**[SECTION 2 --- RIGHT OF FIRST REFUSAL]{.underline}**

**2.1 Company Right of First Refusal.**

**(a) Transfer Notice.** Each Key Holder who proposes to make a Proposed Transfer of Transfer Stock shall deliver a written notice (the \"Transfer Notice\") to the Company not less than thirty (30) days prior to the proposed closing date of such Proposed Transfer. The Transfer Notice shall set forth in reasonable detail: (i) the number of shares of Transfer Stock subject to the Proposed Transfer (the \"Offered Shares\"); (ii) the proposed purchase price per share for the Offered Shares; (iii) the aggregate consideration to be paid for the Offered Shares; (iv) the identity and contact information of the Proposed Transferee; (v) the proposed closing date of the Proposed Transfer; (vi) a summary of the material terms and conditions of the Proposed Transfer, including any representations, warranties, indemnification obligations, or other non-price terms; and (vii) a true, correct, and complete copy of any written agreement, term sheet, letter of intent, or other document relating to the Proposed Transfer. The Transfer Notice shall constitute a binding and irrevocable offer by the Key Holder to sell the Offered Shares to the Company and the Investors on the terms and conditions described in the Transfer Notice, subject to compliance with the procedures set forth in this Section 2 and Section 3, and such offer shall remain open and irrevocable for the periods specified herein.

**(b) Company Notice Period and Exercise.** Upon receipt of the Transfer Notice, the Company shall have a period of fifteen (15) days from the date of its receipt of the Transfer Notice (the \"Company Notice Period\") to elect to purchase all or any portion of the Offered Shares at the price per share and on the terms set forth in the Transfer Notice, by delivering written notice of such election (the \"Company Notice\") to the Key Holder within the Company Notice Period. The Company Notice shall specify the number of Offered Shares that the Company elects to purchase. If the Company does not elect to purchase all of the Offered Shares within the Company Notice Period, the Company shall, promptly upon the expiration of the Company Notice Period (and in any event within two (2) business days thereafter), deliver a copy of the Transfer Notice to each Investor, together with a written notice specifying the number of Offered Shares not purchased by the Company and available for purchase by the Investors pursuant to Section 2.2.

If the Company fails to deliver the Company Notice within the Company Notice Period, the Company shall be deemed to have declined to exercise its Right of First Refusal with respect to all of the Offered Shares, and the Company\'s obligation to forward the Transfer Notice to the Investors pursuant to the preceding sentence shall apply as though the Company had affirmatively declined on the last day of the Company Notice Period.

The right of the Company to purchase Offered Shares pursuant to this Section 2.1 is referred to herein as the \"Right of First Refusal\" or \"ROFR.\"

**2.2 Investor Secondary Right of First Refusal.**

**(a) Investor Notice Period and Exercise.** If the Company does not exercise its Right of First Refusal with respect to all of the Offered Shares pursuant to Section 2.1, each Investor shall have the right (the \"Secondary ROFR\") to purchase its pro rata share of the remaining Offered Shares not purchased by the Company (such remaining shares, the \"Available Shares\"). Each Investor shall have a period of fifteen (15) days from the date of such Investor\'s receipt of the forwarded Transfer Notice from the Company (the \"Investor Notice Period\") to elect to purchase its pro rata share of the Available Shares at the price per share and on the terms set forth in the Transfer Notice, by delivering written notice of such election (the \"Investor Notice\") to the Key Holder and the Company within the Investor Notice Period. The Investor Notice shall specify the number of Available Shares that such Investor elects to purchase.

For purposes of this Section 2.2, an Investor\'s \"pro rata share\" shall be determined by dividing (x) the number of shares of Common Stock then held by such Investor (calculated on an as-converted basis, assuming conversion of all outstanding shares of Preferred Stock held by such Investor into Common Stock) by (y) the aggregate number of shares of Common Stock then held by all Investors (calculated on an as-converted basis, assuming conversion of all outstanding shares of Preferred Stock held by all Investors into Common Stock).

If any Investor fails to deliver an Investor Notice within the Investor Notice Period, such Investor shall be deemed to have declined to exercise its Secondary ROFR with respect to such Investor\'s entire pro rata portion of the Available Shares, and such Investor\'s pro rata share shall be deemed to be available for purchase by the other Investors pursuant to Section 2.2(b) or for sale to the Proposed Transferee subject to Section 2.3 and Section 3.

**(b) Over-Allotment Right.** If any Investor declines or is deemed to have declined to exercise its Secondary ROFR in full, the remaining Investors who have exercised their Secondary ROFR in full shall have the right, for a period of five (5) business days following the expiration of the Investor Notice Period, to purchase the unsubscribed Available Shares on a pro rata basis (based on such exercising Investors\' relative ownership of Common Stock on an as-converted basis among such exercising Investors). To the extent one or more exercising Investors decline the over-allotment opportunity, the other exercising Investors may further elect to purchase such additional shares on the same pro rata basis within the same five (5) business day period. No Investor shall be required to purchase more than the total number of Available Shares.

**2.3 Consummation of Proposed Transfer.**

If the Company and the Investors do not collectively elect to purchase all of the Offered Shares pursuant to Sections 2.1 and 2.2, and subject to the Co-Sale Rights set forth in Section 3, the Key Holder may consummate the Proposed Transfer of the unsubscribed Offered Shares (i.e., those Offered Shares not purchased by the Company or the Investors) to the Proposed Transferee, provided that such transfer is (i) at a price per share no less than the price per share specified in the Transfer Notice, (ii) on terms and conditions no more favorable to the Proposed Transferee than those set forth in the Transfer Notice, and (iii) consummated within ninety (90) days following the expiration of all applicable exercise periods under this Section 2 (including the Over-Allotment period under Section 2.2(b)). If the Key Holder does not consummate such Proposed Transfer within the foregoing ninety (90) day period, the Key Holder\'s right to transfer the Offered Shares shall expire, and the Key Holder must deliver a new Transfer Notice and recommence the procedures under this Section 2 and Section 3 prior to making any subsequent Proposed Transfer.

**[SECTION 3 --- CO-SALE RIGHTS]{.underline}**

**3.1 Co-Sale Right.**

If any Offered Shares are not purchased by the Company or the Investors pursuant to the Right of First Refusal (Section 2.1) or the Secondary ROFR (Section 2.2), each Investor shall have the right (the \"Co-Sale Right\") to participate in the Proposed Transfer on the same terms and conditions as are specified in the Transfer Notice. Each participating Investor may sell up to its pro rata share of the Proposed Transfer, calculated as follows: the number of shares of Common Stock held by such Investor (on an as-converted basis) divided by the aggregate number of shares of Common Stock held by all Key Holders and all participating Investors (on an as-converted basis), multiplied by the total number of Offered Shares to be transferred in the Proposed Transfer.

Each Investor desiring to exercise its Co-Sale Right shall notify the Key Holder and the Company in writing within the Investor Notice Period (i.e., within fifteen (15) days of receipt of the forwarded Transfer Notice from the Company pursuant to Section 2.1(b)). An Investor may exercise its Co-Sale Right in lieu of, or in addition to (to the extent of remaining Available Shares), its Secondary ROFR under Section 2.2. The Key Holder shall use commercially reasonable efforts to cause the Proposed Transferee to remit directly to each participating Investor the portion of the aggregate sale proceeds to which such Investor is entitled by reason of its participation in the Proposed Transfer, and such payment shall be made simultaneously with the closing of the Proposed Transfer. If the Proposed Transferee refuses to purchase shares from any participating Investor on the same terms as the Proposed Transfer, the Key Holder shall not consummate the Proposed Transfer unless the Key Holder first purchases such shares from such Investor on the same terms and conditions as specified in the Transfer Notice.

**3.3 Failure to Honor Co-Sale Right.**

**Section 4.2 --- Designation of Preferred Stock.**

>
> \(b\) **3,200,000 shares** are hereby designated as \"Series B Preferred Stock\"; and

> \(c\) The remaining **3,600,000 shares** of Preferred Stock are undesignated and may be issued from time to time in one or more additional series as determined by the Board of Directors of the Corporation pursuant to a resolution or resolutions providing for such issuance, subject to the limitations and restrictions set forth herein and in accordance with applicable law.

The rights, preferences, privileges, restrictions, and other matters relating to the Series A Preferred Stock and Series B Preferred Stock are as set forth below.

**Section 4.3 --- Rights, Preferences, and Privileges of Series A Preferred Stock.**

The rights, preferences, privileges, restrictions, and other matters relating to the Series A Preferred Stock are as follows:

**4.3.1 --- Liquidation Preference.** (a) In the event of any voluntary or involuntary liquidation, dissolution, or winding up of the Corporation, or any Deemed Liquidation Event (as defined in Article X hereof) (each, a \"Liquidation Event\"), the holders of shares of Series A Preferred Stock then outstanding shall be entitled to receive, out of the assets of the Corporation available for distribution to its stockholders, prior and in preference to any distribution of any of the assets or surplus funds of the Corporation to the holders of Common Stock by reason of their ownership thereof, an amount per share equal to the greater of (i) the Series A Original Issue Price (as defined below), plus any dividends declared but unpaid on such shares, or (ii) the amount per share that would be payable to such holder if all shares of Series A Preferred Stock had been converted to Common Stock immediately prior to such Liquidation Event, taking into account all shares of capital stock of the Corporation on an as-converted basis. The \"Series A Original Issue Price\" shall mean **\$1.50 per share**, subject to appropriate adjustment in the event of any stock dividend, stock split, stock combination, recapitalization, or other similar event affecting the Series A Preferred Stock.

\(b\) The liquidation preference of the Series A Preferred Stock is a **1x non-participating** liquidation preference. For the avoidance of doubt, holders of Series A Preferred Stock are entitled to the greater of their liquidation preference amount or their as-converted share of the proceeds, but not both. The aggregate liquidation preference for all shares of Series A Preferred Stock outstanding as of the date hereof (assuming 3,200,000 shares outstanding) is **\$4,800,000** (exclusive of declared but unpaid dividends).

\(c\) If, upon the occurrence of a Liquidation Event, the assets and funds legally available for distribution among the holders of the Preferred Stock are insufficient to permit full payment to such holders of their respective liquidation preference amounts, then the entire assets and funds of the Corporation legally available for distribution shall be distributed ratably among the holders of Series A Preferred Stock and Series B Preferred Stock in proportion to the aggregate liquidation preference amounts each such holder would otherwise be entitled to receive.

**4.3.2 --- Conversion Rights.** (a) **Optional Conversion.** Each share of Series A Preferred Stock shall be convertible, at the option of the holder thereof, at any time and from time to time, without the payment of additional consideration by the holder thereof, into such number of fully paid and non-assessable shares of Common Stock as is determined by dividing the Series A Original Issue Price by the Series A Conversion Price (as defined below) in effect at the time of conversion. The \"Series A Conversion Price\" shall initially be equal to the Series A Original Issue Price of \$1.50 per share, resulting in an initial conversion ratio of one (1) share of Common Stock for each one (1) share of Series A Preferred Stock. The Series A Conversion Price, and the rate at which shares of Series A Preferred Stock may be converted into shares of Common Stock, shall be subject to adjustment as provided in Article XI hereof.

\(b\) **Automatic Conversion.** Each share of Series A Preferred Stock shall automatically be converted into shares of Common Stock at the then-effective conversion rate upon the earliest of the following events:

> \(i\) the closing of a firm-commitment underwritten public offering pursuant to an effective registration statement under the Securities Act of 1933, as amended (the \"Securities Act\"), in which the aggregate gross proceeds to the Corporation (before deduction of underwriting discounts, commissions, and offering expenses) are at least **\$50,000,000** and the price per share to the public is at least **\$7.50** (as adjusted for any stock dividends, combinations, splits, recapitalizations, or similar events) (a \"Qualified IPO\"); or
>
> \(ii\) the date specified by written consent or agreement of holders of a majority of the then-outstanding shares of Series A Preferred Stock, voting as a separate series.

\(c\) **Mechanics of Conversion.** No fractional shares of Common Stock shall be issued upon conversion of Series A Preferred Stock. In lieu of any fractional shares to which the holder would otherwise be entitled, the Corporation shall pay cash equal to such fraction multiplied by the fair market value of a share of Common Stock as reasonably determined by the Board of Directors. Upon any conversion, the shares of Series A Preferred Stock so converted shall be retired and may not be reissued.

**4.3.3 --- Voting Rights.** Each holder of outstanding shares of Series A Preferred Stock shall be entitled to cast the number of votes equal to the number of whole shares of Common Stock into which the shares of Series A Preferred Stock held by such holder are convertible as of the record date for determining stockholders entitled to vote on such matter. Except as otherwise required by law or as expressly provided by this Certificate of Incorporation, holders of Series A Preferred Stock shall vote together with the holders of Common Stock and the holders of Series B Preferred Stock as a single class on all matters submitted to the stockholders for a vote.

**4.3.4 --- Dividends.** Holders of Series A Preferred Stock shall be entitled to receive, on a pari passu basis with holders of Common Stock (on an as-converted-to-Common-Stock basis), dividends and distributions when and if declared by the Board of Directors out of funds legally available therefor. The Corporation shall not declare, pay, or set aside any dividends on shares of Common Stock unless the holders of Series A Preferred Stock then outstanding shall simultaneously receive a dividend on each outstanding share of Series A Preferred Stock in an amount equal to the dividend that would be received by the holder of the shares of Common Stock into which each such share of Series A Preferred Stock could then be converted. No separate cumulative dividend shall accrue on the Series A Preferred Stock.

**4.3.5 --- Protective Provisions (Series A).** So long as any shares of Series A Preferred Stock remain outstanding, the Corporation shall not, either directly or indirectly by amendment, merger, consolidation, recapitalization, reclassification, or otherwise, do any of the following without (in addition to any other vote required by law or this Certificate of Incorporation) the prior written consent or affirmative vote of the holders of a majority of the then-outstanding shares of Series A Preferred Stock, given in writing or by vote at a meeting, consenting or voting (as the case may be) as a separate class:

> \(a\) alter or change the rights, preferences, or privileges of the shares of Series A Preferred Stock so as to adversely affect such shares;
>
> \(b\) increase or decrease (other than by conversion) the total number of authorized shares of Series A Preferred Stock;
>
> \(c\) authorize or create (by reclassification or otherwise) any new class or series of capital stock having rights, preferences, or privileges senior to or on a parity with the Series A Preferred Stock with respect to liquidation preference, dividends, redemption, or voting;
>
> \(d\) authorize or effect any Deemed Liquidation Event as defined in Article X hereof;
>
> \(e\) amend, alter, or repeal any provision of this Certificate of Incorporation or the Bylaws of the Corporation in a manner that adversely and materially affects the powers, preferences, or special rights of the Series A Preferred Stock; or
>
> \(f\) increase or decrease the authorized number of members of the Board of Directors of the Corporation.

**Section 4.4 --- Rights, Preferences, and Privileges of Series B Preferred Stock.**

The rights, preferences, privileges, restrictions, and other matters relating to the Series B Preferred Stock are as follows:

**4.4.1 --- Liquidation Preference.** (a) In the event of any Liquidation Event, the holders of shares of Series B Preferred Stock then outstanding shall be entitled to receive, out of the assets of the Corporation available for distribution to its stockholders, prior and in preference to any distribution of any of the assets or surplus funds of the Corporation to the holders of Common Stock by reason of their ownership thereof, and pari passu with the holders of Series A Preferred Stock, an amount per share equal to the greater of (i) the Series B Original Issue Price (as defined below), plus any dividends declared but unpaid on such shares, or (ii) the amount per share that would be payable to such holder if all shares of Series B Preferred Stock had been converted to Common Stock immediately prior to such Liquidation Event, taking into account all shares of capital stock of the Corporation on an as-converted basis. The \"Series B Original Issue Price\" shall mean **\$3.75 per share**, subject to appropriate adjustment in the event of any stock dividend, stock split, stock combination, recapitalization, or other similar event affecting the Series B Preferred Stock.

\(b\) The liquidation preference of the Series B Preferred Stock is a **1x non-participating** liquidation preference. For the avoidance of doubt, holders of Series B Preferred Stock are entitled to the greater of their liquidation preference amount or their as-converted share of the proceeds, but not both. The aggregate liquidation preference for all shares of Series B Preferred Stock outstanding as of the date hereof (assuming 3,200,000 shares outstanding) is **\$12,000,000** (exclusive of declared but unpaid dividends).

\(c\) The pari passu ranking of the Series A Preferred Stock and the Series B Preferred Stock means that, in the event of a Liquidation Event, the holders of Series A Preferred Stock and the holders of Series B Preferred Stock shall share ratably in the assets of the Corporation available for distribution in proportion to the full respective liquidation preference amounts to which each such holder would otherwise be entitled, prior to and in preference over any distribution to the holders of Common Stock. If the assets available for distribution are insufficient to permit payment in full of the aggregate liquidation preference amounts of both the Series A Preferred Stock and the Series B Preferred Stock, then the entire assets of the Corporation legally available for distribution shall be distributed among the holders of Series A Preferred Stock and Series B Preferred Stock pro rata based on the aggregate liquidation preference amount each such holder would otherwise be entitled to receive.

\(d\) After payment in full of the applicable liquidation preference amounts to the holders of the Series A Preferred Stock and the Series B Preferred Stock, the remaining assets of the Corporation available for distribution to stockholders shall be distributed among the holders of Common Stock on a pro rata basis.

**4.4.2 --- Conversion Rights.** (a) **Optional Conversion.** Each share of Series B Preferred Stock shall be convertible, at the option of the holder thereof, at any time and from time to time, without the payment of additional consideration by the holder thereof, into such number of fully paid and non-assessable shares of Common Stock as is determined by dividing the Series B Original Issue Price by the Series B Conversion Price (as defined below) in effect at the time of conversion. The \"Series B Conversion Price\" shall initially be equal to the Series B Original Issue Price of \$3.75 per share, resulting in an initial conversion ratio of one (1) share of Common Stock for each one (1) share of Series B Preferred Stock. The Series B Conversion Price, and the rate at which shares of Series B Preferred Stock may be converted into shares of Common Stock, shall be subject to adjustment as provided in Article XI hereof.

\(b\) **Automatic Conversion.** Each share of Series B Preferred Stock shall automatically be converted into shares of Common Stock at the then-effective conversion rate upon the earliest of the following events:

> \(i\) the closing of a firm-commitment underwritten public offering pursuant to an effective registration statement under the Securities Act in which the aggregate gross proceeds to the Corporation (before deduction of underwriting discounts, commissions, and offering expenses) are at least **\$50,000,000** and the price per share to the public is at least **\$11.25** (as adjusted for any stock dividends, combinations, splits, recapitalizations, or similar events) (a \"Qualified IPO\" for purposes of the Series B Preferred Stock); or
>
> \(ii\) the date specified by written consent or agreement of holders of a majority of the then-outstanding shares of Series B Preferred Stock, voting as a separate series.

\(c\) **Mechanics of Conversion.** No fractional shares of Common Stock shall be issued upon conversion of Series B Preferred Stock. In lieu of any fractional shares to which the holder would otherwise be entitled, the Corporation shall pay cash equal to such fraction multiplied by the fair market value of a share of Common Stock as reasonably determined by the Board of Directors. Upon any conversion, the shares of Series B Preferred Stock so converted shall be retired and may not be reissued.

**4.4.3 --- Voting Rights.** Each holder of outstanding shares of Series B Preferred Stock shall be entitled to cast the number of votes equal to the number of whole shares of Common Stock into which the shares of Series B Preferred Stock held by such holder are convertible as of the record date for determining stockholders entitled to vote on such matter. Except as otherwise required by law or as expressly provided by this Certificate of Incorporation, holders of Series B Preferred Stock shall vote together with the holders of Common Stock and the holders of Series A Preferred Stock as a single class on all matters submitted to the stockholders for a vote.

**4.4.4 --- Dividends.** Holders of Series B Preferred Stock shall be entitled to receive, on a pari passu basis with holders of Common Stock (on an as-converted-to-Common-Stock basis), dividends and distributions when and if declared by the Board of Directors out of funds legally available therefor. The Corporation shall not declare, pay, or set aside any dividends on shares of Common Stock unless the holders of Series B Preferred Stock then outstanding shall simultaneously receive a dividend on each outstanding share of Series B Preferred Stock in an amount equal to the dividend that would be received by the holder of the shares of Common Stock into which each such share of Series B Preferred Stock could then be converted. No separate cumulative dividend shall accrue on the Series B Preferred Stock.

**4.4.5 --- Protective Provisions (Series B).** So long as any shares of Series B Preferred Stock remain outstanding, the Corporation shall not, either directly or indirectly by amendment, merger, consolidation, recapitalization, reclassification, or otherwise, do any of the following without (in addition to any other vote required by law or this Certificate of Incorporation) the prior written consent or affirmative vote of the holders of a majority of the then-outstanding shares of Series B Preferred Stock, given in writing or by vote at a meeting, consenting or voting (as the case may be) as a separate class:

> \(a\) alter or change the rights, preferences, or privileges of the shares of Series B Preferred Stock so as to adversely affect such shares;
>
> \(b\) increase or decrease (other than by conversion) the total number of authorized shares of Series B Preferred Stock;
>
> \(c\) authorize or create (by reclassification or otherwise) any new class or series of capital stock having rights, preferences, or privileges senior to the Series B Preferred Stock with respect to liquidation preference, dividends, redemption, or voting;
>
> \(d\) authorize or effect any Deemed Liquidation Event as defined in Article X hereof;
>
> \(e\) amend, alter, or repeal any provision of this Certificate of Incorporation or the Bylaws of the Corporation in a manner that adversely and materially affects the powers, preferences, or special rights of the Series B Preferred Stock;
>
> \(f\) increase or decrease the authorized number of members of the Board of Directors of the Corporation;
>
> \(g\) redeem, purchase, or otherwise acquire (or pay into or set aside for a sinking fund for such purpose) any shares of Common Stock of the Corporation, other than repurchases of shares of Common Stock at the original issuance price thereof (or the then-current fair market value thereof, if lower) from employees, officers, directors, consultants, or other service providers of the Corporation or any subsidiary upon termination of their service relationship with the Corporation pursuant to agreements approved by the Board of Directors; or
>
> \(h\) declare or pay any dividend or make any distribution on any shares of Common Stock of the Corporation.

**Section 4.5 --- Combined Protective Provisions (All Preferred Stock).**

In addition to the series-specific protective provisions set forth in Sections 4.3.5 and 4.4.5 hereof, so long as any shares of Preferred Stock (of any series) remain outstanding, the Corporation shall not, either directly or indirectly by amendment, merger, consolidation, recapitalization, reclassification, or otherwise, do any of the following without (in addition to any other vote required by law or this Certificate of Incorporation) the prior written consent or affirmative vote of the holders of a majority of all then-outstanding shares of Preferred Stock (Series A Preferred Stock and Series B Preferred Stock, voting together as a single class on an as-converted-to-Common-Stock basis):

> \(a\) increase the total number of authorized shares of Common Stock or Preferred Stock of the Corporation;
>
> \(b\) authorize or issue any equity security (including any security convertible into or exercisable for any equity security) that is senior to or on a parity with any existing series of Preferred Stock with respect to dividends, liquidation preference, redemption, or voting, other than shares issued pursuant to the existing authorized but undesignated Preferred Stock in a manner consistent with this Certificate of Incorporation;
>
> \(c\) incur, assume, or guarantee any indebtedness for borrowed money in excess of \$500,000 individually or \$1,000,000 in the aggregate outstanding at any time (excluding trade payables and equipment financing incurred in the ordinary course of business);
>
> \(d\) make any loan or advance to, or guarantee any obligation of, any employee, officer, or director of the Corporation or any subsidiary in excess of \$100,000 in the aggregate (other than reasonable travel advances and similar expenditures in the ordinary course of business); or
>
> \(e\) enter into any transaction or series of related transactions with any director, officer, or holder of more than five percent (5%) of the outstanding capital stock of the Corporation (or any entity controlled by, controlling, or under common control with any such person) (an \"Affiliate Transaction\"), unless such Affiliate Transaction has been approved by a majority of the disinterested members of the Board of Directors.

**Section 4.6 --- Rights of Common Stock.**

The rights, preferences, privileges, and restrictions of the Common Stock are as follows:

\(a\) **Voting.** Each holder of outstanding shares of Common Stock shall be entitled to one (1) vote for each share of Common Stock held by such holder on the record date for the determination of stockholders entitled to vote at each meeting of stockholders of the Corporation and on all matters submitted to a vote of stockholders, except as otherwise required by law or this Certificate of Incorporation. Except as otherwise expressly provided herein or as required by law, the holders of Common Stock shall vote together with the holders of Preferred Stock (on an as-converted basis) as a single class on all matters submitted to a vote of stockholders.

\(b\) **Dividends.** Subject to the prior rights and preferences of the holders of Preferred Stock as set forth in this Certificate of Incorporation, holders of Common Stock shall be entitled to receive dividends and other distributions in cash, stock, or property of the Corporation when, as, and if declared thereon by the Board of Directors from time to time out of assets or funds of the Corporation legally available therefor.

\(c\) **Liquidation.** In the event of any Liquidation Event, after the payment of all preferential amounts required to be paid to the holders of shares of Preferred Stock pursuant to Sections 4.3.1 and 4.4.1 hereof, the remaining assets of the Corporation available for distribution to its stockholders shall be distri

ibuted among the holders of shares of Common Stock, pro rata based on the number of shares held by each such holder.

\(d\) **No Preemptive Rights.** No holder of shares of Common Stock shall be entitled, as a matter of right, to subscribe for, purchase, or receive any part of any new or additional issue of stock of any class or series, or of securities convertible into stock of any class or series, whether now or hereafter authorized and whether issued for cash, property, services, or otherwise, except as may be expressly granted to such holder by a separate written agreement between such holder and the Corporation.

**[ARTICLE V]{.underline}**

**[BOARD OF DIRECTORS]{.underline}**

The Board of Directors of the Corporation shall be composed as follows:

The business and affairs of the Corporation shall be managed by or under the direction of the Board of Directors. **[ARTICLE VI]{.underline}**

**[STOCKHOLDER ACTION]{.underline}**

**Section 6.1 --- Annual and Special Meetings.**

Meetings of stockholders of the Corporation may be held at such place, if any, within or outside the State of Delaware, as may be designated by the Board of Directors from time to time and stated in the notice of the meeting. The Board of Directors may, in its sole discretion, determine that any meeting of stockholders shall not be held at any place but may instead be held solely by means of remote communication as authorized by Section 211(a)(2) of the DGCL. Special meetings of the stockholders of the Corporation may be called at any time by the Board of Directors, the Chairperson of the Board (if any), or the Chief Executive Officer, and shall be called by the Secretary upon the written request of holders of at least twenty-five percent (25%) of the outstanding shares of capital stock entitled to vote at such meeting.

**Section 6.2 --- Action by Written Consent.**

Unless otherwise restricted by this Certificate of Incorporation, any action required or permitted to be taken at any annual or special meeting of stockholders of the Corporation may be taken without a meeting, without prior notice, and without a vote, if a consent or consents in writing, setting forth the action so taken, shall be signed by the holders of outstanding stock having not less than the minimum number of votes that would be necessary to authorize or take such action at a meeting at which all shares entitled to vote thereon were present and voted, and such consent or consents are delivered to the Corporation in accordance with Section 228 of the DGCL.

**[ARTICLE VII]{.underline}**

**[LIMITATION OF LIABILITY]{.underline}**

**Section 7.1 --- Limitation of Director Liability.**

To the fullest extent permitted by the Delaware General Corporation Law as it now exists or as it may hereafter be amended (but, in the case of any such amendment, only to the extent that such amendment permits the Corporation to provide broader limitation of liability than permitted prior thereto), no director of the Corporation shall be personally liable to the Corporation or its stockholders for monetary damages for breach of fiduciary duty as a director; *provided, however*, that this provision shall not eliminate or limit the liability of a director: (i) for any breach of the director\'s duty of loyalty to the Corporation or its stockholders; (ii) for acts or omissions not in good faith or which involve intentional misconduct or a knowing violation of law; (iii) under Section 174 of the Delaware General Corporation Law (relating to unlawful payment of dividends, unlawful stock purchases, or unlawful stock redemptions); or (iv) for any transaction from which the director derived an improper personal benefit. If the DGCL is amended after the date of filing of this Certificate of Incorporation to authorize corporate action further eliminating or limiting the personal liability of directors, then the liability of a director of the Corporation shall be eliminated or limited to the fullest extent permitted by the DGCL, as so amended.

**Section 7.2 --- Amendment.**

Any amendment, repeal, or modification of the foregoing provisions of this Article VII shall not adversely affect any right or protection of a director of the Corporation with respect to any act or omission occurring prior to the time of such amendment, repeal, or modification.

**[ARTICLE VIII]{.underline}**

**[INDEMNIFICATION]{.underline}**

**Section 8.1 --- Right to Indemnification.**

The Corporation shall indemnify, to the fullest extent permitted by applicable law as it presently exists or may hereafter be amended (but, in the case of any such amendment, only to the extent that such amendment permits the Corporation to provide broader indemnification rights than permitted prior thereto), any person (an \"Indemnified Person\") who was or is made a party or is threatened to be made a party to, or is otherwise involved in, any threatened, pending, or completed action, suit, or proceeding, whether civil, criminal, administrative, or investigative (a \"Proceeding\"), by reason of the fact that such person, or a person for whom such person is the legal representative, is or was a director or officer of the Corporation, or while a director or officer of the Corporation is or was serving at the request of the Corporation as a director, officer, employee, or agent of another corporation, partnership, joint venture, trust, enterprise, or nonprofit entity, including service with respect to an employee benefit plan, against all liability, loss, and expense (including attorneys\' fees, judgments, fines, ERISA excise taxes or penalties, and amounts paid in settlement) actually and reasonably incurred or suffered by such Indemnified Person in connection with such Proceeding. Notwithstanding the preceding sentence, the Corporation shall be required to indemnify an Indemnified Person in connection with a Proceeding (or part thereof) commenced by such Indemnified Person only if the commencement of such Proceeding (or part thereof) by the Indemnified Person was authorized by the Board of Directors.

**Section 8.2 --- Advancement of Expenses.**

The Corporation shall, to the fullest extent not prohibited by applicable law, pay the expenses (including attorneys\' fees) incurred by an Indemnified Person in defending any Proceeding in advance of its final disposition; *provided, however*, that, to the extent required by applicable law, such payment of expenses in advance of the final disposition of the Proceeding shall be made only upon receipt of an undertaking by the Indemnified Person to repay all amounts so advanced if it shall ultimately be determined by final judicial decision from which there is no further right to appeal that such Indemnified Person is not entitled to be indemnified for such expenses under this Article VIII or otherwise.

**Section 8.3 --- Non-Exclusivity.**

The rights to indemnification and advancement of expenses conferred by this Article VIII shall not be exclusive of any other right which any person may have or hereafter acquire under any statute, provision of this Certificate of Incorporation, provision of the Bylaws, agreement, vote of stockholders or disinterested directors, or otherwise. The Corporation is specifically authorized to enter into individual contracts with any or all of its directors, officers, employees, or agents respecting indemnification and advancement of expenses, to the fullest extent not prohibited by the DGCL or other applicable law.

**[TRANSFER RESTRICTIONS]{.underline}**

**Section 9.1 --- Board Consent Required for Transfers of Common Stock.**

No holder of Common Stock shall transfer, sell, assign, pledge, hypothecate, or otherwise dispose of any shares of Common Stock of the Corporation (a \"Transfer\") without the prior written consent of the Board of Directors of the Corporation, which consent may be granted or withheld in the sole discretion of the Board. Any purported Transfer of shares of Common Stock without such prior written consent of the Board of Directors shall be void and of no force or effect, and the Corporation shall not be required to recognize any such purported Transfer or register any such purported Transfer on the books and records of the Corporation. The Corporation shall not be obligated to treat as a stockholder of record any purported transferee of shares transferred in violation of this Section 9.1.

For purposes of this Section 9.1, \"Transfer\" shall mean and include any voluntary or involuntary transfer, sale, assignment, pledge, hypothecation, grant of a security interest, encumbrance, or other disposition of shares of Common Stock, whether direct or indirect, including without limitation any transfer by operation of law (including by merger, consolidation, or otherwise), any transfer pursuant to a divorce decree, order of attachment, or other court order, and any transfer of a beneficial interest in shares held in trust or by a nominee. The foregoing definition shall be interpreted broadly to encompass any change in beneficial ownership of shares of Common Stock.

**Section 9.2 --- Exempt Transfers.**

Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 9.1, the following Transfers of shares of Common Stock shall not require the prior written consent of the Board of Directors:

> \(a\) any Transfer of shares of Common Stock to the Corporation itself, including any repurchase of shares by the Corporation from a stockholder pursuant to a stock repurchase agreement or equity incentive plan approved by the Board of Directors;
>
> \(b\) any Transfer of shares of Common Stock by a stockholder to such stockholder\'s spouse, registered domestic partner, parents, children, or grandchildren, or to a trust, limited partnership, limited liability company, or other estate-planning vehicle established for the sole benefit of the stockholder and/or any of the foregoing family members (collectively, \"Permitted Transferees\"); *provided* that the Permitted Transferee shall, as a condition to such Transfer, execute and deliver to the Corporation a written joinder or counterpart signature page to (i) the Right of First Refusal and Co-Sale Agreement, (ii) the Investors\' Rights Agreement, (iii) the Voting Agreement, and (iv) any other stockholder agreement then in effect, agreeing to be bound by the terms thereof as a \"Key Holder\" or \"Stockholder\" (as applicable) to the same extent as the transferring stockholder;
>
> \(c\) any Transfer of shares of Common Stock effected in connection with a Deemed Liquidation Event (as defined in Article X) that has been duly approved by the Board of Directors and the requisite holders of Preferred Stock in accordance with this Certificate of Incorporation and applicable law; and
>
> \(d\) any Transfer of shares of Common Stock effected solely by reason of the conversion of shares of Preferred Stock into shares of Common Stock pursuant to the conversion provisions set forth in this Certificate of Incorporation.

**Section 9.3 --- Compliance with Agreements.**

In addition to the consent requirements of this Article IX, all Transfers of shares of Common Stock shall be subject to, and conditioned upon, compliance with (i) the Right of First Refusal and Co-Sale Agreement among the Corporation and certain of its stockholders (as amended from time to time, the \"ROFR Agreement\"), (ii) the Investors\' Rights Agreement among the Corporation and certain of its stockholders (as amended from time to time, the \"IRA\"), (iii) the Voting Agreement among the Corporation and certain of its stockholders (as amended from time to time), (iv) the Bylaws of the Corporation, and (v) all applicable federal and state securities laws, rules, and regulations. No Transfer shall be effective unless and until the transferring stockholder has complied with all applicable provisions of the foregoing agreements and governing documents, in addition to the consent requirement set forth in Section 9.1 hereof.

**Section 9.4 --- Legends.**

Each certificate representing shares of Common Stock or Preferred Stock of the Corporation (or, if shares are held in book-entry form, each book-entry notation or statement of holdings) shall bear the following legends (or legends substantially similar in form and substance):

> \(a\) \"THE SHARES REPRESENTED BY THIS CERTIFICATE HAVE NOT BEEN REGISTERED UNDER THE SECURITIES ACT OF 1933, AS AMENDED, OR UNDER ANY STATE SECURITIES LAWS, AND MAY NOT BE OFFERED, SOLD, TRANSFERRED, PLEDGED, OR OTHERWISE DISPOSED OF EXCEPT PURSUANT TO AN EFFECTIVE REGISTRATION STATEMENT UNDER SUCH ACT AND APPLICABLE STATE SECURITIES LAWS OR PURSUANT TO AN APPLICABLE EXEMPTION FROM THE REGISTRATION REQUIREMENTS OF SUCH ACT AND SUCH LAWS.\"
>
> \(b\) \"THE SHARES REPRESENTED BY THIS CERTIFICATE ARE SUBJECT TO CERTAIN RESTRICTIONS ON TRANSFER AND OTHER TERMS AND CONDITIONS AS SET FORTH IN THE AMENDED AND RESTATED CERTIFICATE OF INCORPORATION OF THE CORPORATION, THE BYLAWS OF THE CORPORATION, AND CERTAIN AGREEMENTS TO WHICH THE CORPORATION AND THE HOLDER OF SUCH SHARES ARE PARTIES, INCLUDING A RIGHT OF FIRST REFUSAL AND CO-SALE AGREEMENT, AN INVESTORS\' RIGHTS AGREEMENT, AND A VOTING AGREEMENT, COPIES OF WHICH ARE ON FILE AT THE PRINCIPAL OFFICE OF THE CORPORATION. NO TRANSFER OF SUCH SHARES SHALL BE EFFECTIVE UNLESS AND UNTIL THE TERMS AND CONDITIONS OF SUCH INSTRUMENTS HAVE BEEN COMPLIED WITH IN FULL.\"
>
> \(c\) Any legend required by applicable state securities or \"blue sky\" laws of any state in which the stockholder resides.

**[ARTICLE X]{.underline}**

**[DEEMED LIQUIDATION EVENTS]{.underline}**

**Section 10.1 --- Definition.**

For purposes of this Certificate of Incorporation, a \"Deemed Liquidation Event\" shall mean any of the following events, unless the holders of a majority of the then-outstanding shares of Preferred Stock (voting together as a single class on an as-converted basis) elect otherwise by written notice given to the Corporation at least five (5) days prior to the effective date of any such event:

> \(a\) a merger or consolidation (other than one in which the holders of capital stock of the Corporation outstanding immediately prior to such merger or consolidation continue to hold at least fifty percent (50%) of the voting power of the surviving or acquiring entity or its parent immediately following such transaction);
>
> \(b\) a sale, lease, transfer, exclusive license, or other disposition, in a single transaction or series of related transactions, by the Corporation or any subsidiary of the Corporation of all or substantially all of the assets of the Corporation and its subsidiaries taken as a whole, except where such sale, lease, transfer, exclusive license, or other disposition is to a wholly owned subsidiary of the Corporation; or
>
> \(c\) any transaction or series of related transactions (including without limitation any reorganization, merger, consolidation, or share transfer) the result of which is that holders of the Corporation\'s capital stock immediately prior thereto cease to own more than fifty percent (50%) of the voting power of the Corporation or, if such transaction results in a parent entity of the Corporation, such parent entity.

**Section 10.2 --- Treatment of Deemed Liquidation Events.**

In the event of a Deemed Liquidation Event, the consideration payable to the stockholders of the Corporation (or, in the case of a Deemed Liquidation Event described in Section 10.1(b), the consideration received by the Corporation) shall be distributed to the holders of the Corporation\'s capital stock in the same manner and order of priority as a distribution of assets upon a voluntary liquidation, dissolution, or winding up of the Corporation pursuant to Sections 4.3.1 and 4.4.1 hereof, as applicable, with the Preferred Stock liquidation preferences being satisfied first (pari passu among Series A and Series B) and the remaining proceeds distributable to the holders of Common Stock. The Corporation shall give each holder of Preferred Stock written notice of any proposed Deemed Liquidation Event not less than twenty (20) days prior to the closing or effective date thereof.

**[ARTICLE XI]{.underline}**

**[ANTI-DILUTION PROVISIONS]{.underline}**

**Section 11.1 --- Weighted Average Anti-Dilution.**

\(a\) If the Corporation issues additional shares of Common Stock, or rights, options, warrants, or other securities convertible into or exercisable or exchangeable for shares of Common Stock (collectively, \"Additional Shares\"), without consideration or for a consideration per share (or having a conversion or exercise price per share) less than the applicable Conversion Price then in effect for any series of Preferred Stock immediately prior to such issuance (a \"Dilutive Issuance\"), then and in each such event, the applicable Conversion Price for each affected series of Preferred Stock shall be reduced, concurrently with such Dilutive Issuance, to a price determined by application of the following broad-based weighted average formula:

> **CP₂ = CP₁ × (A + B) / (A + C)**

Where:

> **CP₂** = the adjusted Conversion Price immediately following the Dilutive Issuance;
>
> **CP₁** = the Conversion Price in effect immediately prior to the Dilutive Issuance;
>
> **A** = the number of shares of Common Stock outstanding immediately prior to such Dilutive Issuance, calculated on a fully diluted, as-converted basis (including all shares of Common Stock issuable upon conversion of all outstanding shares of Preferred Stock and all shares of Common Stock reserved for issuance under any equity incentive plan, whether or not then subject to outstanding options or other awards);
>
> **B** = the number of additional shares of Common Stock that the aggregate consideration received (or deemed received) by the Corporation for the total number of Additional Shares actually issued in such Dilutive Issuance would purchase at CP₁ (i.e., aggregate consideration ÷ CP₁);
>
> **C** = the number of Additional Shares actually issued (or deemed issued) in such Dilutive Issuance.

\(b\) **Excluded Issuances.** Notwithstanding the foregoing, no adjustment to the applicable Conversion Price shall be made upon the issuance of any of the following (collectively, \"Excluded Issuances\"):

> \(i\) shares of Common Stock (or options or other rights to purchase shares of Common Stock) issued to employees, officers, directors, consultants, advisors, or other service providers of the Corporation or any subsidiary pursuant to any equity incentive plan, stock purchase plan, or other compensatory arrangement duly approved by the Board of Directors of the Corporation, provided that the aggregate number of shares reserved under all such plans does not exceed the number of shares approved by the Board and the requisite stockholders;
>
> \(ii\) shares of Common Stock issued upon the conversion of any shares of Preferred Stock;
>
> \(iii\) shares of Common Stock issued upon the exercise or conversion of any options, warrants, or convertible securities outstanding as of the date of filing of this Certificate of Incorporation;
>
> \(iv\) shares of Common Stock (or options, warrants, or convertible securities) issued in connection with bona fide strategic transactions (including joint ventures, licensing transactions, technology partnerships, or similar arrangements) approved by the Board of Directors and the holders of a majority of the outstanding Preferred Stock (voting together as a single class on an as-converted basis); and
>
> \(v\) shares of Common Stock issued in connection with a Qualified IPO.

**[ARTICLE XII]{.underline}**

**[REDEMPTION]{.underline}**

**Section 12.1 --- No Mandatory Redemption.**

The shares of Preferred Stock of the Corporation are not subject to mandatory redemption. The Corporation shall not be required to redeem or repurchase any shares of Preferred Stock at any time or upon the occurrence of any event, and no holder of Preferred Stock shall have any right to require the Corporation to redeem or repurchase any shares of Preferred Stock.

**[ARTICLE XIII]{.underline}**

**[MISCELLANEOUS]{.underline}**

**Section 13.1 --- Amendments.**

This Amended and Restated Certificate of Incorporation may be amended, altered, or repealed only in the manner prescribed by the Delaware General Corporation Law and, to the extent required by this Certificate of Incorporation, with the prior written consent or affirmative vote of the requisite holders of Preferred Stock as set forth in the applicable protective provisions of Sections 4.3.5, 4.4.5, and 4.5 hereof. Any proposed amendment that would adversely and materially affect any particular series of Preferred Stock shall require the separate consent of the holders of a majority of the then-outstanding shares of such series, as provided herein.

**Section 13.2 --- Severability.**

If any provision of this Certificate of Incorporation, or the application of such provision to any person or circumstance, is held invalid, illegal, or unenforceable in any respect by a court of competent jurisdiction, such invalidity, illegality, or unenforceability shall not affect any other provision hereof, and the remaining provisions of this Certificate of Incorporation shall remain in full force and effect.

**Section 13.3 --- Governing Law.**

This Certificate of Incorporation shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the internal laws of the State of Delaware, without regard to any conflict-of-law provisions that would require the application of the laws of any other jurisdiction.
