**[AMENDED AND RESTATED BYLAWS OF MERIDIAN BOLT TECHNOLOGIES, INC.]{.underline}**

A Delaware Corporation

Originally adopted: March 14, 2019 Amended and Restated effective as of August 22, 2022

These Amended and Restated Bylaws of Meridian Bolt Technologies, Inc. (the \"Corporation\") are adopted in connection with the Corporation\'s Series B financing and pursuant to the Amended and Restated Certificate of Incorporation of Meridian Bolt Technologies, Inc., as filed with the Secretary of State of the State of Delaware. These Bylaws amend, restate, and supersede in their entirety all prior bylaws of the Corporation and shall govern the conduct of the Corporation\'s business and affairs from and after the effective date set forth above.

**[ARTICLE I --- OFFICES]{.underline}**

**[Section 1.1 --- Registered Office]{.underline}**

The registered office of the Corporation in the State of Delaware shall be located at such place as is set forth in the Certificate of Incorporation of the Corporation, as the same may be amended from time to time. The registered agent of the Corporation in the State of Delaware shall be the agent named in the Certificate of Incorporation.

**[Section 1.2 --- Principal Office]{.underline}**

The principal office of the Corporation shall be located at 2200 Castlegate Boulevard, Suite 400, Austin, TX 78746, or at such other place, either within or without the State of Delaware, as the Board of Directors may from time to time designate by resolution.

**[Section 1.3 --- Other Offices]{.underline}**

The Corporation may also maintain such additional offices and places of business, within or without the State of Delaware, as the Board of Directors may from time to time determine or as the business of the Corporation may require.

**[ARTICLE II --- MEETINGS OF STOCKHOLDERS]{.underline}**

**[Section 2.1 --- Place of Meetings]{.underline}**

Meetings of stockholders shall be held at such place, if any, either within or without the State of Delaware, as may be designated from time to time by the Board of Directors and stated in the notice of meeting. The Board of Directors may, in its sole discretion, determine that any meeting of stockholders shall be held solely by means of remote communication to the fullest extent permitted by applicable law.

**[Section 2.2 --- Annual Meetings]{.underline}**

An annual meeting of stockholders shall be held on such date, at such time, and at such place, if any, as shall be determined by the Board of Directors and set forth in the notice of meeting. At the annual meeting, the stockholders shall elect directors and transact such other business as may properly be brought before the meeting in accordance with applicable law, the Certificate of Incorporation, and these Bylaws.

**[Section 2.3 --- Special Meetings]{.underline}**

Special meetings of stockholders may be called at any time by the Board of Directors, the Chairperson of the Board, if one has been elected, or the Chief Executive Officer. Special meetings may also be called by the Secretary upon the written request of the holders of not less than ten percent (10%) of the outstanding shares of capital stock entitled to vote at such meeting. Business transacted at any special meeting shall be limited to the matters stated in the notice of meeting.

**[Section 2.4 --- Notice of Meetings]{.underline}**

Written notice of each meeting of stockholders, whether annual or special, shall be given in accordance with applicable law not less than ten (10) days nor more than sixty (60) days before the date of the meeting to each stockholder entitled to vote at such meeting. Such notice shall state the place, if any, date, and hour of the meeting, the means of remote communication, if any, by which stockholders and proxy holders may be deemed to be present in person and vote at such meeting, and, in the case of a special meeting, the purpose or purposes for which the meeting is called. Notice shall be given in the manner provided in Article XII of these Bylaws.

**[Section 2.5 --- Quorum]{.underline}**

Except as otherwise required by law, the Certificate of Incorporation, or these Bylaws, the holders of a majority of the shares of capital stock issued and outstanding and entitled to vote at a meeting, present in person or represented by proxy, shall constitute a quorum for the transaction of business at all meetings of stockholders. If a quorum shall not be present or represented at any meeting of stockholders, the chairperson of the meeting or the holders of a majority of the shares present in person or represented by proxy may adjourn the meeting from time to time to another time and/or place without further notice other than announcement at the meeting, unless notice is required by law.

**[Section 2.6 --- Voting]{.underline}**

Except as otherwise provided by law, the Certificate of Incorporation, or these Bylaws, each stockholder shall be entitled to one vote for each share of capital stock held by such stockholder and entitled to vote thereon. All elections of directors shall be determined by a plurality of the votes cast by the shares present in person or represented by proxy and entitled to vote on the election of directors. All other matters brought before any meeting of stockholders shall be decided by the affirmative vote of a majority of the shares present in person or represented by proxy and entitled to vote on the subject matter.

**[Section 2.7 --- Proxies]{.underline}**

Each stockholder entitled to vote at a meeting of stockholders may authorize another person or persons to act for such stockholder by proxy in any manner permitted by the Delaware General Corporation Law. Such proxy shall be filed with the Secretary of the Corporation before or at the time of the meeting. No proxy shall be voted or acted upon after three (3) years from its date, unless the proxy expressly provides for a longer period.

**[Section 2.8 --- Action Without Meeting]{.underline}**

Any action required or permitted to be taken at any annual or special meeting of stockholders may be taken without a meeting, without prior notice, and without a vote, if a consent or consents in writing, setting forth the action so taken, shall be signed by the holders of outstanding stock having not less than the minimum number of votes that would be necessary to authorize or take such action at a meeting at which all shares entitled to vote thereon were present and voted. Such consents shall be delivered to the Corporation in the manner required by the Delaware General Corporation Law. Prompt notice of the taking of corporate action without a meeting by less than unanimous written consent shall be given to those stockholders who have not consented in writing and who would have been entitled to notice of the meeting if such action had been taken at a meeting.

**[Section 2.9 --- Record Date]{.underline}**

In order that the Corporation may determine the stockholders entitled to notice of or to vote at any meeting of stockholders, the Board of Directors may fix a record date, which shall not precede the date upon which the resolution fixing the record date is adopted and which shall not be more than sixty (60) nor less than ten (10) days before the date of such meeting. If no record date is fixed by the Board of Directors, the record date shall be determined in accordance with the Delaware General Corporation Law.

**[ARTICLE III --- BOARD OF DIRECTORS]{.underline}**

**[Section 3.1 --- Powers]{.underline}**

The business and affairs of the Corporation shall be managed by or under the direction of the Board of Directors. In addition to the powers and authorities expressly conferred upon it by these Bylaws and the Certificate of Incorporation, the Board of Directors may exercise all such powers of the Corporation and do all such lawful acts and things as are not by statute, the Certificate of Incorporation, or these Bylaws required to be exercised or done by the stockholders.

**[Section 3.2 --- Number and Qualification]{.underline}**

The number of directors constituting the entire Board of Directors shall be five (5), unless otherwise changed by amendment to the Certificate of Incorporation or by resolution duly adopted by the Board of Directors to the extent permitted by the Certificate of Incorporation. Directors need not be stockholders of the Corporation and need not be residents of the State of Delaware. As of the effective date of these Bylaws, the Board of Directors consists of five (5) members.

**[Section 3.3 --- Election and Term]{.underline}**

Directors shall be elected at each annual meeting of stockholders and shall hold office until the next annual meeting of stockholders and until their respective successors are duly elected and qualified, or until such director\'s earlier resignation, removal, or death. The composition of the Board of Directors shall be as set forth in the Certificate of Incorporation, including any rights of the holders of Preferred Stock or any series thereof to designate one or more directors.

**[Section 3.4 --- Vacancies]{.underline}**

Any vacancy occurring on the Board of Directors, including any vacancy resulting from the death, resignation, removal, disqualification, or incapacity of a director, or from an increase in the authorized number of directors, may be filled by the affirmative vote of a majority of the remaining directors then in office, although less than a quorum, or by the sole remaining director, except as otherwise required by law or the Certificate of Incorporation. Any director so chosen to fill a vacancy shall hold office for the remainder of the full term of the class, if any, in which the vacancy occurred and until such director\'s successor shall have been duly elected and qualified.

**[Section 3.5 --- Resignation and Removal]{.underline}**

Any director may resign at any time by giving written notice to the Corporation. Such resignation shall take effect at the time specified therein, or, if no time is specified, upon receipt thereof by the Corporation. Directors may be removed, with or without cause, to the extent and in the manner provided in the Certificate of Incorporation and the Delaware General Corporation Law.

**[Section 3.6 --- Regular Meetings]{.underline}**

Regular meetings of the Board of Directors may be held at such times and at such places, within or without the State of Delaware, as shall from time to time be determined by resolution of the Board of Directors. Notice of regular meetings need not be given.

**[Section 3.7 --- Special Meetings]{.underline}**

Special meetings of the Board of Directors may be called by the Chairperson of the Board, if any, the Chief Executive Officer, or any two (2) directors. Notice of each special meeting shall be given to each director at least forty-eight (48) hours before the time of the meeting if delivered personally, by telephone, or by electronic transmission, or at least five (5) days before the time of the meeting if delivered by mail. Notice of any special meeting need not specify the purpose of the meeting unless otherwise required by law, the Certificate of Incorporation, or these Bylaws.

**[Section 3.8 --- Quorum and Voting]{.underline}**

A majority of the total number of directors then in office shall constitute a quorum for the transaction of business at any meeting of the Board of Directors. Except as otherwise required by law, the Certificate of Incorporation, or these Bylaws, the act of a majority of the directors present at any meeting at which a quorum is present shall be the act of the Board of Directors. If a quorum shall not be present at any meeting of the Board of Directors, a majority of the directors present may adjourn the meeting from time to time until a quorum shall be present.

**[Section 3.9 --- Action Without Meeting]{.underline}**

Any action required or permitted to be taken at any meeting of the Board of Directors or of any committee thereof may be taken without a meeting if all members of the Board of Directors or such committee, as the case may be, consent thereto in writing or by electronic transmission, and the writing or writings or electronic transmission or transmissions are filed with the minutes of proceedings of the Board or committee.

**[Section 3.10 --- Telephonic Meetings]{.underline}**

Members of the Board of Directors or any committee designated by the Board may participate in a meeting of the Board or such committee by means of conference telephone or other communications equipment by means of which all persons participating in the meeting can hear one another. Participation in a meeting pursuant to this Section 3.10 shall constitute presence in person at such meeting.

**[Section 3.11 --- Committees]{.underline}**

The Board of Directors may, by resolution adopted by a majority of the entire Board, designate one or more committees, each committee to consist of one or more directors of the Corporation, to the extent permitted by law. The Board may designate one or more directors as alternate members of any committee, who may replace any absent or disqualified member at any meeting of such committee. In the absence or disqualification of any member of a committee, the member or members thereof present at a meeting and not disqualified from voting, whether or not such member or members constitute a quorum, may unanimously appoint another member of the Board of Directors to act at the meeting in place of any absent or disqualified member. Any such committee, to the extent provided in the resolution of the Board and permitted by law, shall have and may exercise the powers and authority of the Board of Directors.

**[Section 3.12 --- Compensation]{.underline}**

Unless otherwise restricted by the Certificate of Incorporation, the Board of Directors shall have authority to fix the compensation of directors. Directors may be paid such compensation for their services and may be reimbursed for expenses of attendance at each meeting of the Board of Directors or any committee thereof, as the Board may from time to time determine.

**[Section 3.13 --- Interested Directors]{.underline}**

No contract or transaction between the Corporation and one or more of its directors or officers, or between the Corporation and any other corporation, partnership, association, or other organization in which one or more of its directors or officers are directors or officers, or have a financial interest, shall be void or voidable solely for this reason, or solely because the director or officer is present at or participates in the meeting of the Board of Directors or committee thereof which authorizes the contract or transaction, or solely because the vote or votes of such director or officer are counted for such purpose, if:

> \(a\) the material facts as to such director\'s or officer\'s relationship or interest and as to the contract or transaction are disclosed or are known to the Board of Directors or the committee, and the Board of Directors or committee in good faith authorizes the contract or transaction by the affirmative votes of a majority of the disinterested directors, even though the disinterested directors be less than a quorum;
>
> \(b\) the material facts as to such director\'s or officer\'s relationship or interest and as to the contract or transaction are disclosed or are known to the stockholders entitled to vote thereon, and the contract or transaction is specifically approved in good faith by vote of the stockholders; or
>
> \(c\) the contract or transaction is fair as to the Corporation as of the time it is authorized, approved, or ratified by the Board of Directors, a committee thereof, or the stockholders.

Common or interested directors may be counted in determining the presence of a quorum at a meeting of the Board of Directors or of a committee which authorizes such contract or transaction. This Section 3.13 is intended to be consistent with, and shall be interpreted in a manner consistent with, Section 144 of the Delaware General Corporation Law, as the same may be amended from time to time.

**[ARTICLE IV --- OFFICERS]{.underline}**

**[Section 4.1 --- Designation of Officers]{.underline}**

The officers of the Corporation shall include a Chief Executive Officer, a President, a Secretary, and a Treasurer or Chief Financial Officer. The offices of Chief Executive Officer and President may be held by the same person. The Board of Directors may also appoint a Chief Technology Officer, one or more Vice Presidents, one or more Assistant Secretaries, one or more Assistant Treasurers, and such other officers and agents as the Board of Directors shall deem necessary or advisable. Any number of offices may be held by the same person, except as otherwise prohibited by law.

**[Section 4.2 --- Election and Term]{.underline}**

The officers of the Corporation shall be elected by the Board of Directors at such time or times as the Board may determine. Each officer shall hold office until such officer\'s successor shall have been duly elected and qualified, or until such officer\'s earlier resignation, removal, or death.

**[Section 4.3 --- Chief Executive Officer]{.underline}**

The Chief Executive Officer shall be the principal executive officer of the Corporation and shall, subject to the control of the Board of Directors, have general supervision, direction, and control of the business and affairs of the Corporation. Unless the Board of Directors has elected a separate Chairperson of the Board, the Chief Executive Officer shall preside at all meetings of the stockholders and at all meetings of the Board of Directors at which the Chief Executive Officer is present. The Chief Executive Officer shall have the general powers and duties of management usually vested in the office of chief executive officer of a corporation and shall have such other powers and duties as may from time to time be prescribed by the Board of Directors.

**[Section 4.4 --- Chief Technology Officer]{.underline}**

The Chief Technology Officer, if one is appointed, shall be responsible for the technology vision, architecture, strategy, research, and development activities of the Corporation, in each case subject to the supervision and direction of the Chief Executive Officer and the Board of Directors. The Chief Technology Officer shall perform such additional duties and shall have such further powers as may from time to time be prescribed by the Board of Directors or the Chief Executive Officer.

**[Section 4.5 --- Secretary]{.underline}**

The Secretary shall attend all meetings of the Board of Directors and all meetings of the stockholders and shall record the proceedings of such meetings in books or records maintained for that purpose. The Secretary shall give, or cause to be given, notice of all meetings of stockholders and all special meetings of the Board of Directors and shall perform such other duties as may be prescribed by the Board of Directors or the Chief Executive Officer. The Secretary shall have custody of the corporate seal, if any, and shall have authority to affix the same to any instrument requiring it and, when so affixed, to attest the same. The Secretary shall also maintain, or cause to be maintained, the stock ledger and transfer records of the Corporation.

**[Section 4.6 --- Treasurer / Chief Financial Officer]{.underline}**

The Treasurer, or if designated by the Board of Directors the Chief Financial Officer, shall have custody of the corporate funds and securities and shall keep, or cause to be kept, full and accurate accounts of receipts and disbursements in books belonging to the Corporation. The Treasurer or Chief Financial Officer shall deposit all monies and other valuable effects in the name and to the credit of the Corporation in such depositories as may be designated by the Board of Directors. The Corporation\'s banking relationship shall be maintained at Lone Star National Bank or at such other financial institution or institutions as the Board of Directors may from time to time designate. The Treasurer or Chief Financial Officer shall disburse the funds of the Corporation as may be ordered by the Board of Directors and shall render to the Chief Executive Officer and the Board, whenever requested, an account of all financial transactions and of the financial condition of the Corporation.

**[Section 4.7 --- Removal and Resignation]{.underline}**

Any officer may be removed, with or without cause, by the Board of Directors at any time. Any officer may resign at any time by giving written notice to the Corporation. Such resignation shall take effect upon the date of receipt of such notice or at any later time specified therein, and unless otherwise specified therein, acceptance of such resignation shall not be necessary to make it effective.

**[ARTICLE V --- CAPITAL STOCK]{.underline}**

**[Section 5.1 --- Certificates]{.underline}**

Shares of the Corporation\'s capital stock may be represented by certificates or may be uncertificated, as provided under the Delaware General Corporation Law and as determined by the Board of Directors. Each holder of stock represented by certificates shall be entitled to a certificate signed by, or in the name of, the Corporation by any two (2) authorized officers of the Corporation, certifying the number and class of shares owned by such stockholder in the Corporation. Any or all signatures on any certificate may be facsimile signatures. Every certificate representing shares of capital stock, and every notice or statement issued with respect to uncertificated shares, shall bear or contain such legends or notices as may be required by law and shall reference any restrictions on transfer imposed by the Certificate of Incorporation, these Bylaws, or any agreement to which the Corporation is a party.

**[Section 5.2 --- Stock Ledger]{.underline}**

The Corporation shall maintain a stock ledger, which may be maintained by the Secretary, the Treasurer, an authorized transfer agent, or such other person as the Board of Directors may designate. The stock ledger shall contain the name and address of each stockholder, the number and class or series of shares held by each stockholder, the certificate number or numbers of certificated shares, if any, and the date of issuance of such shares. The stock ledger shall be the only evidence as to who are the stockholders entitled to examine the stock ledger, the list required by Section 219 of the Delaware General Corporation Law, or the books of the Corporation, or to vote in person or by proxy at any meeting of stockholders.

**[Section 5.3 --- Transfers of Stock]{.underline}**

Transfers of shares of stock of the Corporation shall be made only on the stock ledger of the Corporation by the holder of record thereof, or by such holder\'s attorney duly authorized in writing, upon surrender of the certificate or certificates for such shares, if certific

cated, properly endorsed or accompanied by a stock power duly executed, together with such proof of the authenticity of signatures and such other evidence of authority as the Corporation or its transfer agent may reasonably require. In the case of uncertificated shares, transfers shall be made in accordance with applicable law and the procedures established by the Corporation or its transfer agent.

No transfer of shares shall be valid as against the Corporation for any purpose until it shall have been entered in the stock ledger of the Corporation. No transfer of shares shall be effective unless and until all applicable transfer restrictions set forth in the Certificate of Incorporation, these Bylaws, and any agreement between the Corporation and the holder of such shares (including, without limitation, any Right of First Refusal and Co-Sale Agreement, Investors\' Rights Agreement, or similar agreement) have been complied with or duly waived. The Corporation may place appropriate stop-transfer instructions on its books and records or with any transfer agent in order to enforce the provisions of this Section 5.3 and any applicable transfer restrictions.

**[Section 5.4 --- Record Holders]{.underline}**

The Corporation shall be entitled to recognize the exclusive right of a person registered on its books as the owner of shares to receive dividends, to vote as such owner, and to hold all other rights of a stockholder of record, and shall not be bound to recognize any equitable or other claim to or interest in such share or shares on the part of any other person, whether or not it shall have express or other notice thereof, except as otherwise required by law.

**[Section 5.5 --- Lost Certificates]{.underline}**

The Board of Directors may direct that a new certificate or certificates be issued in place of any certificate or certificates theretofore issued by the Corporation alleged to have been lost, stolen, or destroyed, upon the making of an affidavit of that fact by the person claiming the certificate to be lost, stolen, or destroyed. When authorizing the issuance of a new certificate or certificates, the Board of Directors may, in its discretion and as a condition precedent to such issuance, require the owner of the lost, stolen, or destroyed certificate or certificates, or such owner\'s legal representative, to give the Corporation a bond in such sum and with such surety or sureties as the Board may direct as indemnity against any claim that may be made against the Corporation with respect to the certificate alleged to have been lost, stolen, or destroyed.

**[ARTICLE VI --- DIVIDENDS AND DISTRIBUTIONS]{.underline}**

**[Section 6.1 --- Declaration of Dividends]{.underline}**

Subject to the provisions of applicable law and the Certificate of Incorporation, dividends upon the capital stock of the Corporation may be declared by the Board of Directors at any regular or special meeting of the Board. Dividends may be paid in cash, in property, or in shares of the Corporation\'s capital stock, subject in each case to the provisions of the Certificate of Incorporation.

**[Section 6.2 --- Reserves]{.underline}**

Before payment of any dividend, there may be set aside out of any funds of the Corporation available for dividends such reserve or reserves as the Board of Directors from time to time, in its absolute discretion, deems proper for any lawful or proper purpose, and the Board of Directors may modify or abolish any such reserve in the manner in which it was created.

**[ARTICLE VII --- RESTRICTIONS ON TRANSFER OF SECURITIES]{.underline}**

**[Section 7.1 --- General Transfer Restrictions]{.underline}**

No stockholder shall sell, assign, transfer, pledge, hypothecate, or otherwise dispose of, whether voluntarily, involuntarily, by operation of law, or otherwise (collectively, a \"Transfer\"), any shares of capital stock of the Corporation, or any interest therein, except in compliance with the provisions of this Article VII, the Certificate of Incorporation, and any applicable stockholders\' agreement, investors\' rights agreement, right of first refusal and co-sale agreement, or similar agreement to which such stockholder and the Corporation are parties. Any purported Transfer in violation of this Article VII shall be null and void and of no force or effect, and the Corporation shall not register, record, or otherwise recognize any such Transfer on its stock ledger or books and records.

**[Section 7.2 --- Board Approval Required]{.underline}**

No Transfer of shares of Common Stock shall be effective unless and until the Board of Directors has approved such Transfer by the affirmative vote of a majority of the Board of Directors. The Board of Directors may, in its sole discretion, approve or deny any proposed Transfer for any reason or for no reason, subject only to applicable law and any contrary provision in the Certificate of Incorporation or any applicable agreement binding upon the Corporation. Any request for approval of a proposed Transfer shall be submitted to the Secretary of the Corporation in writing and shall specify, at a minimum, the number of shares proposed to be transferred, the identity of the proposed transferee, the proposed price per share or other consideration, and all other material terms and conditions of the proposed Transfer. The Secretary shall promptly provide such request to the Board of Directors for consideration.

**[Section 7.3 --- Preferred Stockholder Consent for Significant Transfers]{.underline}**

Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in these Bylaws, any Transfer of shares of Common Stock by a single stockholder or group of affiliated stockholders that, in a single transaction or a series of related transactions, would result in the Transfer of more than five percent (5%) of the total number of shares of Common Stock then issued and outstanding shall require, in addition to the approval of the Board of Directors pursuant to Section 7.2, the prior written consent of the holders of a majority of the then-outstanding shares of Preferred Stock, voting together as a single class on an as-converted basis.

For purposes of this Section 7.3, the number of shares of Common Stock then issued and outstanding shall be calculated as of the date of the Transfer notice submitted to the Board of Directors pursuant to Section 7.2, without giving effect to any options, warrants, or other convertible securities.

The Corporation shall not register or record any Transfer on its stock ledger, and no such Transfer shall be effective or recognized by the Corporation, unless and until the requisite consent of the holders of Preferred Stock has been obtained in accordance with this Section 7.3.

**[Section 7.4 --- Exempt Transfers]{.underline}**

The following Transfers shall be exempt from the approval requirements of Sections 7.2 and 7.3 of these Bylaws:

> \(a\) any Transfer of shares to the Corporation itself, including any repurchase, redemption, or similar reacquisition by the Corporation;
>
> \(b\) any Transfer effected pursuant to a merger, consolidation, recapitalization, reorganization, or other business combination transaction that has been approved by the Board of Directors and, to the extent required by law or the Certificate of Incorporation, by the stockholders of the Corporation;
>
> \(c\) any Transfer by operation of law, including a Transfer to the executor, administrator, personal representative, guardian, conservator, or similar fiduciary of a deceased or legally incapacitated stockholder\'s estate, provided that any such transferee shall take and hold the transferred shares subject to all restrictions on transfer applicable to such shares under these Bylaws and any applicable agreement; and
>
> \(d\) any Transfer by a stockholder to such stockholder\'s Immediate Family Members or to a trust, family limited partnership, limited liability company, or similar estate-planning vehicle for the benefit of the stockholder or one or more of the stockholder\'s Immediate Family Members, provided that, as a condition to the effectiveness of such Transfer, the transferee agrees in writing, in form and substance reasonably satisfactory to the Corporation, to be bound by the terms of these Bylaws and any applicable stockholders\' agreements, investors\' rights agreements, right of first refusal and co-sale agreements, or similar agreements.

For purposes of this Section 7.4, \"Immediate Family Members\" means a stockholder\'s spouse, domestic partner, parents, children, and siblings. No exemption under this Section 7.4 shall be construed to exempt any Transfer from compliance with any applicable stockholders\' agreement, investors\' rights agreement, right of first refusal and co-sale agreement, applicable federal or state securities law restriction, or any other transfer restriction binding upon the shares or the transferring stockholder.

**[Section 7.5 --- Legends]{.underline}**

Each certificate representing shares of capital stock of the Corporation, and each book-entry or other notation representing uncertificated shares, shall bear or include such legends as may be required by applicable law and as may be determined by the Board of Directors from time to time. Without limiting the foregoing, such legends may include, without limitation, references to: (a) the transfer restrictions set forth in this Article VII; (b) any applicable right of first refusal and co-sale agreement; (c) any applicable investors\' rights agreement; (d) any restrictions arising under applicable federal and state securities laws; and (e) such other matters as the Board of Directors may determine are necessary or appropriate to give notice of restrictions affecting the shares.

**[ARTICLE VIII --- INDEMNIFICATION]{.underline}**

**[Section 8.1 --- Right to Indemnification]{.underline}**

The Corporation shall indemnify and hold harmless, to the fullest extent permitted by applicable law as it presently exists or may hereafter be amended, any person who was or is made, or is threatened to be made, a party to or is otherwise involved in any threatened, pending, or completed action, suit, arbitration, alternative dispute resolution proceeding, inquiry, hearing, investigation, or other proceeding, whether civil, criminal, administrative, or investigative (a \"Proceeding\"), by reason of the fact that such person, or a person for whom such person is the legal representative, is or was a director or officer of the Corporation or, while serving as a director or officer of the Corporation, is or was serving at the request of the Corporation as a director, officer, employee, or agent of another corporation, partnership, limited liability company, joint venture, trust, employee benefit plan, or other enterprise (a \"Covered Person\"), against all liability and loss suffered and expenses, including attorneys\' fees, judgments, fines, excise taxes, and amounts paid in settlement, actually and reasonably incurred by such Covered Person in connection with such Proceeding. Notwithstanding the foregoing, except as provided in Section 8.3 with respect to proceedings to enforce rights to indemnification or advancement, the Corporation shall be required to indemnify a Covered Person in connection with a Proceeding initiated by such Covered Person only if such Proceeding was authorized in advance by the Board of Directors.

**[Section 8.2 --- Advancement of Expenses]{.underline}**

The Corporation shall pay the expenses, including attorneys\' fees, incurred by a Covered Person in defending or otherwise participating in any Proceeding in advance of its final disposition; provided, however, that such payment of expenses incurred by a Covered Person in advance of the final disposition of the Proceeding shall be made only upon receipt by the Corporation of an undertaking by or on behalf of the Covered Person to repay all amounts so advanced if it shall ultimately be determined that the Covered Person is not entitled to be indemnified under this Article VIII or otherwise.

**[Section 8.3 --- Claims]{.underline}**

If a claim for indemnification under Section 8.1 or for advancement of expenses under Section 8.2 is not paid in full by the Corporation within sixty (60) days after a written claim therefor has been received by the Corporation, the Covered Person may file suit to recover the unpaid amount of such claim. If successful in whole or in part in any such suit, or in a suit brought by the Corporation to recover an advancement of expenses pursuant to the terms of an undertaking, the Covered Person shall be entitled to be paid also the expense of prosecuting or defending such suit. In any action brought pursuant to this Section 8.3, the Corporation shall have the burden of proving that the Covered Person is not entitled to the requested indemnification or advancement of expenses under applicable law.

**[Section 8.4 --- Non-Exclusivity]{.underline}**

The rights conferred on any Covered Person by this Article VIII shall not be exclusive of any other rights which such Covered Person may have or hereafter acquire under any statute, provision of the Certificate of Incorporation, these Bylaws, agreement, vote of stockholders or disinterested directors, or otherwise. The rights provided by this Article VIII shall be deemed contract rights and shall continue as provided herein.

**[Section 8.5 --- Insurance]{.underline}**

The Corporation may purchase and maintain insurance, at its expense, on behalf of any person who is or was a director, officer, employee, or agent of the Corporation, or who is or was serving at the request of the Corporation as a director, officer, employee, agent, fiduciary, or similar representative of another corporation, partnership, limited liability company, joint venture, trust, employee benefit plan, or other enterprise, against any liability asserted against such person and incurred by such person in any such capacity, or arising out of such person\'s status as such, whether or not the Corporation would have the power to indemnify such person against such liability under the provisions of this Article VIII or the Delaware General Corporation Law.

**[Section 8.6 --- Survival]{.underline}**

The rights to indemnification and advancement of expenses provided by, or granted pursuant to, this Article VIII shall continue as to a person who has ceased to be a Covered Person and shall inure to the benefit of the heirs, executors, administrators, legal representatives, and estate of such person.

**[ARTICLE IX --- BOOKS AND RECORDS]{.underline}**

**[Section 9.1 --- Books and Records]{.underline}**

The Corporation shall keep at its principal office, or at such other place or places as the Board of Directors may order, correct and complete books and records of account, minutes of the proceedings of stockholders, the Board of Directors, and any committees of the Board, and the stock ledger and a current list of stockholders of the Corporation. The Corporation\'s books and records shall be maintained in such form as the Board of Directors may determine, including in written form or in any other form capable of being converted into written form within a reasonable time. The Corporation\'s books and records shall be audited annually by an independent certified public accounting firm. As of the effective date of these Bylaws, the Corporation\'s external auditors are Thornfield Accounting Group LLP, or such other independent certified public accounting firm as the Board of Directors may from time to time designate.

**[Section 9.2 --- Inspection of Records]{.underline}**

Any stockholder, in person or by attorney or other agent, shall, upon written demand under oath stating the purpose thereof, have the right during the usual hours for business to inspect for any proper purpose, and to make copies and extracts from, the Corporation\'s stock ledger, a list of its stockholders, and its other books and records, in each case as permitted by and subject to the conditions and limitations set forth in the Delaware General Corporation Law.

**[ARTICLE X --- FISCAL YEAR]{.underline}**

**[Section 10.1 --- Fiscal Year]{.underline}**

The fiscal year of the Corporation shall end on December 31 of each year, unless otherwise fixed from time to time by resolution of the Board of Directors.

**[ARTICLE XI --- CORPORATE SEAL]{.underline}**

**[Section 11.1 --- Corporate Seal]{.underline}**

The Board of Directors may adopt a corporate seal in such form as the Board shall determine. The corporate seal may be used by causing it, or a facsimile thereof, to be impressed, affixed, stamped, printed, or otherwise reproduced on any instrument or document as the Board or any authorized officer may determine.

**[ARTICLE XII --- NOTICES]{.underline}**

**[Section 12.1 --- Manner of Notice]{.underline}**

Whenever notice is required to be given to any stockholder, director, or officer under the provisions of these Bylaws, the Certificate of Incorporation, or applicable law, such notice may be given in writing by personal delivery, by deposit in the United States mail with first class postage prepaid, by nationally recognized overnight courier, by facsimile transmission, or by electronic transmission, including electronic mail, to such person at the address, facsimile number, or electronic mail address, as the case may be, as it appears on the records of the Corporation or as otherwise provided by such person to the Corporation for notice purposes.

**[Section 12.2 --- Waiver of Notice]{.underline}**

Whenever notice is required to be given under any provision of these Bylaws, the Certificate of Incorporation, or applicable law, a written waiver thereof, signed by the person entitled to notice, whether before or after the time stated therein, or a waiver by electronic transmission by the person entitled to notice, shall be deemed equivalent to notice. Attendance of a person at a meeting shall constitute a waiver of notice of such meeting, except when such person attends a meeting for the express purpose of objecting, at the beginning of the meeting, to the transaction of any business because the meeting is not lawfully called or convened. Neither the business to be transacted at, nor the purpose of, any regular or special meeting of stockholders, directors, or members of a committee of directors need be specified in any written waiver of notice unless so required by law.

**[ARTICLE XIII --- AMENDMENTS]{.underline}**

**[Section 13.1 --- Amendments by Board]{.underline}**

These Bylaws may be altered, amended, or repealed, and new bylaws may be adopted, by the Board of Directors at any regular or special meeting of the Board. The Board of Directors shall have the power to adopt, amend, or repeal bylaws, provided that notice of the proposed alteration, amendment, repeal, or adoption has been given in accordance with the notice provisions applicable to special meetings of the Board under these Bylaws.

**[Section 13.2 --- Amendments by Stockholders]{.underline}**

Notwithstanding Section 13.1, the stockholders of the Corporation shall also have the power to adopt, amend, or repeal these Bylaws at any annual or special meeting of stockholders, provided that notice of the proposed action is contained in the notice of such meeting. Any bylaw adopted, amended, or repealed by the stockholders may thereafter be amended or repealed by the Board of Directors, unless the resolution of the stockholders adopting or amending such bylaw expressly provides that such bylaw may not be amended or repealed by the Board of Directors.

**[Section 13.3 --- Protective Provisions]{.underline}**

Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in this Article XIII or elsewhere in these Bylaws, no amendment, repeal, or modification of Article VII (Restrictions on Transfer of Securities) of these Bylaws, and no adoption of any provision inconsistent therewith, shall be effective without the prior written consent of the holders of a majority of the then-outstanding shares of Preferred Stock, voting together as a single class on an as-converted basis.

**[ARTICLE XIV --- GENERAL PROVISIONS]{.underline}**

**[Section 14.1 --- Governing Law]{.underline}**

These Bylaws and all questions relating to their validity, interpretation, enforcement, and application shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of Delaware, without giving effect to any choice or conflict of law provision or rule that would cause the application of the laws of any jurisdiction other than the State of Delaware.

**[Section 14.2 --- Severability]{.underline}**

If any provision of these Bylaws shall be held to be invalid, illegal, or unenforceable for any reason whatsoever, the validity, legality, and enforceability of the remaining provisions of these Bylaws shall not in any way be affected or impaired thereby, and, to the fullest extent possible, the provisions of these Bylaws shall be construed so as to preserve the intent manifested by the provision held invalid, illegal, or unenforceable.

**[Section 14.3 --- Construction]{.underline}**

Unless the context otherwise requires, the general provisions, rules of construction, and definitions contained in the Delaware General Corporation Law shall govern the construction of these Bylaws. Without limiting the generality of the foregoing, words in the singular shall include the plural, and words in the plural shall include the singular. All references in these Bylaws to the word \"including\" shall be deemed to mean \"including, without limitation.\"

**[Section 14.4 --- Definitions]{.underline}**

Capitalized terms used but not otherwise defined in these Bylaws shall have the meanings ascribed to such terms in the Certificate of Incorporation. References in these Bylaws to the \"Certificate of Incorporation\" shall mean the Amended and Restated Certificate of Incorporation of the Corporation, as the same may be amended, restated, supplemented, or otherwise modified from time to time.

**[Section 409A Valuation --- Executive Summary]{.underline}**

**[Fair Market Value Determination of Common Stock]{.underline}**

**Meridian Bolt Technologies, Inc.**

Valuation Date: June 15, 2024

Prepared by: Winterhaven Colton & Associates 200 Spear Street, Suite 1500 San Francisco, CA 94105

\ 

This report is confidential and has been prepared solely for the Board of Directors and management of Meridian Bolt Technologies, Inc. for purposes of compliance with Section 409A of the Internal Revenue Code. This report should not be used for any other purpose or relied upon by any third party without the prior written consent of Winterhaven Colton & Associates.

**[Section 1: Engagement Overview and Purpose]{.underline}**

Winterhaven Colton & Associates (\"BCA\") was engaged by Meridian Bolt Technologies, Inc. (the \"Company\"), a Delaware C-corporation incorporated on March 14, 2019 and headquartered at 2200 Castlegate Boulevard, Suite 400, Austin, TX 78746, to perform an independent valuation of the Company\'s common stock (\$0.0001 par value per share) as of June 15, 2024 (the \"Valuation Date\").

The purpose of the valuation is to determine the fair market value (\"FMV\") of the Company\'s common stock for purposes of compliance with Section 409A of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended (the \"Code\"), and the regulations promulgated thereunder. The FMV determination is intended to be used by the Company in connection with the granting of stock options and other equity compensation awards under the Company\'s 2021 Equity Incentive Plan. The Company develops industrial automation and predictive-maintenance software-as-a-service (\"SaaS\") products for commercial and industrial customers.

In preparing this valuation, BCA has relied upon financial statements, management-prepared projections, capitalization records, equity agreements, and other information provided by the Company\'s management. BCA has not independently audited or verified such information. The Company\'s external auditors are Thornfield Accounting Group LLP. This executive summary presents the key findings and conclusions of BCA\'s full valuation report.

**[Section 2: Conclusion of Value]{.underline}**

**Based upon BCA\'s analysis, the fair market value of one share of common stock of Meridian Bolt Technologies, Inc. as of June 15, 2024 is \$4.82 per share.**

This conclusion represents the FMV of the Company\'s common stock on a per-share, minority, non-marketable basis. The concluded value reflects the application of a Discount for Lack of Marketability (\"DLOM\") of 25% to the equity value allocated to common stock through the Option Pricing Method, as described further in Section 5 below.

The conclusion of value is based upon BCA\'s assessment of the Company\'s capitalization structure, historical and projected financial performance, prevailing market conditions, and data from comparable publicly traded companies, all as of the Valuation Date. BCA\'s analysis considers the rights, preferences, and privileges of each class of the Company\'s outstanding equity securities and allocates the total equity value among such classes accordingly.

This valuation is valid for a period of up to twelve (12) months from the Valuation Date (i.e., through June 15, 2025), provided that no material events occur that would reasonably be expected to affect the value of the Company\'s equity during such period. Material events that could affect the continued validity of this valuation include, but are not limited to, new equity financing rounds, significant changes in revenue trajectory or business model, acquisitions or dispositions, or secondary transactions in the Company\'s securities at prices materially different from the concluded FMV.

**[Section 3: Capitalization Summary]{.underline}**

As of the Valuation Date, the Company\'s authorized and outstanding capital structure is summarized below.

**Authorized Capital:**

  -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Class**               **Authorized Shares**   **Par Value**
  ----------------------- ----------------------- -----------------------
  Common Stock            25,000,000              \$0.0001

  Preferred Stock         10,000,000              \$0.0001
  -----------------------------------------------------------------------

**Outstanding Equity Securities:**

  -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Class**                  **Shares Outstanding**   **Issue Date**     **Price Per Share**   **Aggregate Investment**   **Liquidation Preference**
  -------------------------- ------------------------ ------------------ --------------------- -------------------------- -------------------------------------
  Common Stock               8,200,000                Various            Various               ---                        ---

  Series A Preferred Stock   3,200,000                January 10, 2021   \$1.50                \$4,800,000                \$4,800,000 (1x non-participating)

  Series B Preferred Stock   3,200,000                August 22, 2022    \$3.75                \$12,000,000               \$12,000,000 (1x non-participating)

  **Total Preferred**        **6,400,000**                                                     **\$16,800,000**           **\$16,800,000**
  -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The Series A financing round was led by Ridgeline Ventures, L.P. The Series B financing round was led by Verdana Growth Partners III, L.P. Both series of preferred stock carry a 1x non-participating liquidation preference.

**Equity Incentive Plan:**

The Company\'s 2021 Equity Incentive Plan authorizes the issuance of up to 2,500,000 shares of common stock. As of the Valuation Date, 1,800,000 options have been granted under the plan (of which 1,200,000 are vested and 600,000 remain unvested), and 700,000 shares remain available for future grants.

**Fully Diluted Share Count:**

  -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Component**                                   **Shares**
  ----------------------------------------------- -----------------------------------
  Common Stock Outstanding                        8,200,000

  Preferred Stock Outstanding (as-converted)      6,400,000

  Equity Incentive Plan (total authorized pool)   2,500,000

  **Fully Diluted Total**                         **17,100,000**
  -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The total aggregate liquidation preferences of all outstanding preferred stock equal \$16,800,000 (\$4,800,000 for Series A and \$12,000,000 for Series B).

**[Section 4: Valuation Methodology]{.underline}**

BCA employed the **Option Pricing Method (\"OPM\") Backsolve** approach as the primary valuation methodology for determining the fair market value of the Company\'s common stock. The OPM Backsolve is a widely accepted and commonly applied methodology for valuing equity securities of privately held venture-backed companies with complex capital structures involving multiple classes of stock with differing rights and preferences.

**OPM Backsolve Approach.** The OPM Backsolve method uses the most recent arm\'s-length round of equity financing as a calibration anchor and then solves for the total equity value of the Company that is consistent with the price paid in that financing round, given the Company\'s capital structure and the rights, preferences, and privileges of each class of equity. In this case, BCA used the Series B Preferred Stock financing, which closed on August 22, 2022 at a price of \$3.75 per share of Series B Preferred Stock (aggregate investment of \$12,000,000), as the anchor transaction. The OPM treats each class of equity (common stock, Series A Preferred Stock, Series B Preferred Stock, and the option pool) as a call option on the total enterprise value of the Company, with exercise prices (or \"breakpoints\") determined by the aggregate liquidation preferences and participation rights of each class.

**Key Inputs to the OPM:**

  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Parameter**                       **Value**
  ----------------------------------- ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Series B Price Per Share            \$3.75

  Series B Aggregate Investment       \$12,000,000

  Time to Liquidity Assumption        3.5 years from Valuation Date (estimated late 2027 / early 2028)

  Risk-Free Rate                      4.65% (U.S. Treasury yield, comparable maturity, as of June 15, 2024)

  Equity Volatility                   55% (based on comparable publicly traded SaaS and industrial technology companies)
  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

**Corroborating Methodology.** BCA also considered the **Income Approach** (discounted cash flow analysis) as a secondary corroborating methodology. Under the Income Approach, BCA projected the Company\'s future free cash flows based on management-prepared financial projections and discounted those cash flows to present value using a risk-adjusted discount rate. The results of the Income Approach were broadly consistent with the equity value implied by the OPM Backsolve, thereby providing additional support for BCA\'s concluded value.

**Market Approach.** BCA considered but did not rely upon a Market Approach using comparable company revenue or EBITDA multiples. BCA determined that the difficulty of identifying a sufficiently comparable set of publicly traded peers --- given the Company\'s early-stage status, hybrid industrial automation and SaaS business model, and scale --- made the Market Approach less reliable as a primary methodology in this case.

**Secondary Transactions.** BCA did not have access to any pending or contemplated secondary sale transactions involving the Company\'s common stock as of the Valuation Date and was not made aware of any arm\'s-length offers for the Company\'s common or preferred stock. Accordingly, no secondary transaction data was incorporated into BCA\'s analysis.

**[Section 5: Discount for Lack of Marketability]{.underline}**

BCA applied a **Discount for Lack of Marketability (\"DLOM\") of 25%** to the per-share value of common stock derived from the OPM allocation. The DLOM reflects the inherent illiquidity and restricted transferability of the Company\'s common stock, which is not publicly traded on any securities exchange and is subject to significant contractual and legal transfer restrictions, including:

> \(a\) Restrictions under the Company\'s Amended and Restated Certificate of Incorporation, which require board consent for any transfer of common stock;
>
> \(b\) A Right of First Refusal and Co-Sale Agreement dated August 22, 2022, among the Company, certain stockholders, and the investors;
>
> \(c\) An Investors\' Rights Agreement dated August 22, 2022, which includes market standoff and lock-up provisions applicable to all common stockholders;
>
> \(d\) Transfer restrictions under the Company\'s Amended and Restated Bylaws; and
>
> \(e\) Restrictions under applicable federal and state securities laws, including Rule 144 limitations.

The 25% DLOM was determined based on BCA\'s analysis of restricted stock studies, pre-IPO discount studies, and the Finnerty put-option model, calibrated for the Company\'s estimated time to liquidity of approximately 3.5 years and equity volatility of 55%.

Prior to application of the DLOM, the OPM allocated a per-share value to common stock of approximately **\$6.43**. After application of the 25% DLOM, the resulting per-share FMV of common stock is calculated as follows:

> \$6.43 × (1 − 0.25) = \$6.43 × 0.75 = **\$4.82** (rounded)

The concluded FMV of \$4.82 per share therefore reflects the full impact of the marketability discount as applied to the pre-discount allocated value per share of common stock.

**[Section 6: Key Assumptions and Limiting Conditions]{.underline}**

The conclusion of value set forth in this report is subject to the following key assumptions and limiting conditions:

1\. BCA relied upon financial statements, projections, capitalization information, and other data provided by the Company\'s management. BCA did not independently audit or verify this information. The Company\'s external auditors are Thornfield Accounting Group LLP. BCA assumed that all information provided by management was complete, accurate, and fairly presented in all material respects.

2\. The valuation is based on economic, market, and Company-specific conditions as of the Valuation Date (June 15, 2024). Significant changes in these conditions subsequent to the Valuation Date could materially affect the conclusion of value.

3\. **The conclusion of value assumes no material changes in the Company\'s business, financial condition, or capital structure between the Valuation Date and the date on which the valuation is used for Section 409A purposes. Material events that could affect the continued validity of this valuation include, without limitation: new equity financing rounds, significant revenue growth or decline, changes in competitive position, acquisition offers or indications of interest, secondary transactions in the Company\'s securities at prices materially different from the concluded FMV, or changes in general economic or market conditions.**

4\. This valuation does not constitute a recommendation to purchase or sell shares of the Company\'s stock and should not be relied upon for purposes other than Section 409A compliance, including without limitation for purposes of estate and gift tax, financial reporting, or transaction pricing.

5\. BCA is independent of the Company. Neither BCA nor any of its principals or employees has a financial interest in the Company\'s equity, and BCA\'s compensation for this engagement is not contingent upon the results of the valuation.

6\. This executive summary is provided for convenience only. The conclusion of value is subject to the detailed assumptions, methodologies, qualifications, and limiting conditions set forth in BCA\'s full valuation report, which is incorporated herein by reference.

**[Section 7: Certification and Signature]{.underline}**

BCA hereby certifies that this valuation was prepared in accordance with the requirements of Section 409A of the Internal Revenue Code, IRS Notice 2005-1, and the final Treasury Regulations under Section 409A, including Treasury Regulation §1.409A-1(b)(5)(iv). BCA further certifies that it is qualified to perform this valuation and has significant experience in valuing privately held technology companies for Section 409A and other regulatory purposes.

This valuation constitutes a \"qualified independent appraisal\" within the meaning of Treasury Regulation §1.409A-1(b)(5)(iv)(B)(1), performed by a qualified independent appraiser. As such, the fair market value determined herein creates a rebuttable presumption of reasonableness for purposes of Section 409A of the Code. The presumption applies to any stock option or equity award granted at an exercise price equal to or greater than the concluded FMV of \$4.82 per share, provided the valuation remains valid at the time of grant in accordance with the conditions stated herein.

Title: Senior Managing Director

Winterhaven Colton & Associates 200 Spear Street, Suite 1500 San Francisco, CA 94105

No third party may rely upon this report or the conclusions stated herein without the prior written consent of Winterhaven Colton & Associates. © 2024 Winterhaven Colton & Associates. All rights reserved.
